specFirst: Written BEFORE the code, per skills/agentsBestPractices.md §1. This file, spec.md and README.md are the design record. The plan was approved by the product owner on 2026-09-02 (session plan: binary-purring-lobster) and is restated here; when behaviour must change, change this file first, then the code.
description: Given an explicit catalogProject and the reference of an existing page .defs.ts, decides which molecule (group + tag) serves each region of that page and rewrites the SAME .defs.ts in place — a `molecule: { group, tag }` field on the relevant dataBindings/inputs, plus the chosen molecules' source files and usage contract appended to pipeline[0].dependsFiles/skills. Writes nothing else: no report, no l4 artifact, no trace file. A sibling of agentChooseMolecules (the probe that only measures), built to actually annotate a page.
principles: ZERO ARTIFACT RULE. The only file this agent ever writes is the target .defs.ts (steps/c3-patch). Every handoff between steps travels through the task tree's own step `result` field (helpers/cm2Types.cm2ReadC1Result / cm2ReadGroupResult) — never a file. No report.json, no c1-groups.json, no per-attempt trace, no l4 folder anywhere, in any project.

EXPLICIT CATALOG, NO DISCOVERY. catalogProject arrives in the mention argument. There is no dependency search, no chChooseCatalog, no 'more than one catalog reachable' ambiguity — all of that existed in the probe only because it never received the project.

REGIONS ARE DETERMINISTIC, NEVER INVENTED. helpers/cm2Regions.extractRegions walks the target's own dataBindings[]/inputs[] (kind 'query' -> a view region; a command input with presentation 'form' -> an entry region). No LLM ever decides what counts as a region — c1-groups only decides which GROUP covers a region already handed to it.

THE CATALOG IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF TAGS. Same anti-invention gate as agentChooseMolecules, imported unchanged from its steps/c1-groups/gate.ts and steps/c2-molecules/gate.ts — a tag outside the group's published list is refused by a deterministic gate, never completed by code.

ONE CATALOG LEVEL PER PROMPT. c1 sees level 1 (the group list); each c2 sees level 2 of ONE group. Same funnel and the same reason as the probe (flow.json.principles there): the whole catalog does not fit a prompt.

PERSISTED SHAPE IS MINIMAL. The .defs.ts only ever gets `molecule: { group, tag }` — no reason, no scenarioUsed, no gate history. Those exist transiently inside the run (LLM output, gate checks) and are never written anywhere.

decisions.argument: The whole mention is one JSON object, '{"catalogProject": N, "target": "..."}', parsed with plain JSON.parse (helpers/cm2Entry.cm2ParseEntry) — the same choice agentChangeFrontend's 'only-materialize' command already made for a single flat-object argument. Both keys required; no free prose, no optional-prefix-plus-prose shape (unlike agentChooseMolecules's chParseEntry), so there is no reason to reach for mls.common.safeParseArgs or hand-rolled brace-matching.
decisions.bootstrap: Deterministic (skipRootLLM: true on the initial add-message-ai), same gesture as agentChangeFrontend.ts's beforePromptImplicit. There is no c0-classify: nothing here needs classifying, and the run does not want to spend a call on it.
decisions.regionGranularity: FOUR kinds; the last two were added 2026-09-04. (1) surface: one per query dataBinding — the list/table/selector of its rows, at `binding.id`. (2) entry: one per 'form' input of a command — the control the user types into, at `binding.id::inputName`. (3) trigger: one per COMMAND dataBinding — the control that executes it, also at `binding.id` (a binding is a query or a command, never both, so on a query `molecule` means the surface and on a command the trigger — no new shape needed). (4) page: a need serving the whole page, at `page::<role>`, written to the root pageMolecules[] — today only `page::feedback`, emitted when the page has at least one command. 'selection'/'route' inputs are never regions (populated by picking a row elsewhere, or by the URL), but their COUNT is stated in the surface's need, because a list whose rows feed a command's selected id is a selector rather than a passive table.
decisions.pageMoleculeShape: 2026-09-04: a region serving the WHOLE page has no binding node to carry `molecule`, so it lands in a ROOT array — `pageMolecules: [{ role, group, tag }]` — addressed by the region id `page::<role>` (unambiguous: every binding id this platform generates starts with `binding.`). ARRAY WITH A ROLE, not one field per role (`moleculeFeedback`, `moleculeConfirmation`, ...), because destructive-confirmation and workflow-progress are already known roles and a vocabulary grows without changing the shape; the vocabulary is CLOSED and extended deliberately, holding `feedback` only today. ROOT, not nested under `presentation` (where categoryRef lives): `presentation` is agentChangeFrontend's object, and this agent's output inside it would be exposed to a partial rewrite by its owner — at the root, pageMolecules is unambiguously this agent's, the same clarity of ownership `molecule` has inside a binding, which had no alternative. Safe typewise: `definition` carries no `satisfies` (unlike `pipeline`, which is `as const`). Reconciliation is per role — a rerun replaces its own role and keeps the others; answering none for the last role deletes the key rather than leaving `pageMolecules: []`.
decisions.triggerRegion: 2026-09-04, measured by running the probe and this agent on the SAME file (_102046_ clientCatalogue/page21): the probe found 12 regions to this agent's 7, and 3 of the 5 it could not see were the buttons executing cmdCreateClient/cmdUpdateClient/cmdDeleteClient — which the probe routed to groupTriggerAction, an entire group unreachable from here. Sharpest case: cmdDeleteClient has NO 'form' input (its only input is the selected id), so the whole command binding produced zero regions and vanished from the answer. A command's own trigger is as much a molecule-serving interaction as any field, and it is fully derivable — every command binding has exactly one. After the fix the same file yields 10 regions, covering 10 of the probe's 12.
decisions.typeResolution: Field types come from the sibling web/contracts/{page} file: its .defs.ts first (source of truth), a regex fallback over its compiled .ts when the .defs.ts is not on disk (confirmed necessary on a real client project, mls-102046, where only the .ts was present locally). An unresolved type is honestly 'unknown', never guessed from the field name — same rule the catalog's own usage guidance already states.
decisions.patchTarget: The SAME file passed in target — page11, page12 or any future genome sharing the { definition, pipeline } shape. This agent does not decide which genome gets molecules; whoever calls it decides which file to point at.
decisions.modelType: reasoning + x-tool-strict on both LLM steps (c1-groups, c2-molecules), per skills/modelTypes.md and the agentChooseMolecules precedent. No classifier model anywhere.
decisions.retry: One retry with the gate errors in the prompt (CM2_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2), same budget as the probe. A c2 that still fails after 2 attempts records ok:false and completes — c3-patch leaves that group's regions untouched rather than failing the whole run.
decisions.idempotency: c3-patch compares the rewritten source to the original before writing; a rerun that changes nothing touches no file at all. A region already annotated is reconciled (overwritten or removed), never duplicated.
decisions.projectContext: 2026-09 addendum, measured on _102046_/approveChangeOrder: c2 (not c1 — group choice does not need locale) also reads the TARGET project's own l5/project.json (helpers/cm2ProjectContext.ts) for its declared language(s), added as a 'Project context' prompt section. This is what lets c2 pick between locale-bound siblings (e.g. groupEnterMoney's en-US vs pt-BR molecules) instead of correctly-but-avoidably answering 'none' for lack of any signal. Still a DECLARED fact, never an inference — same category as the contract's own field types, just sourced from l5. Absent/unreadable l5/project.json -> the section is omitted, never padded with a default.
decisions.pageContextC1: 2026-09-04, SUPERSEDES the 'c1 was left alone' decision below: c1 now gets {{pageContext}} too. The earlier reasoning was that c1 had no measured defect — but comparing against the probe on clientCatalogue/page21 showed it does: c1 sent the client list to groupViewTable while the probe sent it to groupSelectOne (ml-listbox-sidebar-select), and the target's own pageObjective declares 'master-detail list with contextual selection' plus the anti-pattern 'Usar um seletor livre de identificadores para editar ou excluir'. A list whose rows feed a command's selected id is a SELECTOR, and groupSelectOne is where the selector siblings live (it even publishes ml-table-single-select). c1 was not correct, it was correct-looking in isolation.
decisions.pageContext: 2026-09-04 addendum, from a measured instability: across two runs of the SAME page, c1 chose the right group every time and c2 flip-flopped inside it — ml-data-table vs ml-view-table (11 siblings), ml-multiline-text vs ml-enter-text (8), ml-radio-group vs nothing (12) — while groupEnterMoney (2 siblings) stayed stable. Instability scaling with sibling count is the signature of missing discriminating evidence, and the catalog was NOT the gap: groupViewTable's skill text ships 10 scenario rows, 11 full descriptions and their layout axes. The gap was the mechanical `need` line, which matched only the catch-all scenario row ('Listagem geral com ordenação e paginação' — which recommends 10 of 11). FIX: c2 now also reads the target page's own declared intent (helpers/cm2PageContext.ts) — purpose, presentation.categoryRef and, on the goal-first genomes, the whole pageObjective (jobToBeDone, primaryDecision, usageFrequency, decisiveInfo, informationHierarchy, antiPatterns, criticalActions[].presentation) — plus one structural fact counted from the defs: how many command inputs are fed by a row selection. ~2.3KB on the measured page, against a 2-6KB group catalog. Read FRESH from the target in c2 rather than threaded through c1's result (which every later step reads). c1 was deliberately LEFT ALONE: it was already 100% correct on both runs, and changing a step with no measured defect is how a fix becomes a regression (agentsBestPractices: 'structural refactors ship with identical external behavior'). page11 has no pageObjective, so there the section degrades to purpose+categoryRef; a defs declaring none of it gets no section at all.
decisions.needLine: 2026-09-04: cm2Regions also states, per entry region, the input's declared `required` flag and HOW MANY typed (presentation:'form') fields the same command has — a one-field command is a single decision, a five-field one is a form, and that changes which sibling fits. Both are facts the defs already carries and this agent was discarding. Still nothing inferred from a field name.
decisions.referenceForm: 2026-09-04, measured then corrected: TWO reference forms exist and are not interchangeable. IMPORT form ('/_102020_/.../usage' — leading slash, no extension) is what `await import()` takes and what a group's index.defs.ts publishes in `usageContract`. PIPELINE form ('_102020_/.../usage.ts' — no leading slash, with extension) is what pipeline[].skills/dependsFiles take. This agent was writing the import form into the pipeline, and agentCfeMaterializeGen SILENTLY dropped every such entry (readSections/readContextSections skip an empty read), so a usage contract that never reached the model was indistinguishable from one never listed: 4 of 6 skills and 6 of 8 dependsFiles were lost. Every reference this agent puts in a pipeline array now goes through cm2Types.cm2PipelineRef. Target form settled by the platform's own generator, not by inference: across every .defs.ts agentChangeFrontend wrote in a real client project, no pipeline reference carries a leading slash. Consequence for the render skill (genCfePage21RenderTs): the runtime import is now built from the dependsFiles entry by prepending '/' and swapping '.ts' for '.js', not by appending '.js'.

conventions.target: An import-style reference to a page .defs.ts, e.g. '_102046_/l2/buildFlowFsm/web/desktop/page11/approveChangeOrder.defs' — decoded by agentChooseMolecules's chFileRefFromImport (reused, not duplicated). Must resolve to extension '.defs.ts'.
conventions.contractPath: Derived from target: same project/level, folder truncated at and including its 'web' segment plus 'contracts', same shortName. Generic across any device/layout naming (page11, page21, mobile, ...).
conventions.handoff: c1's result carries { catalogProject, target, regions, groups } forward; each c2's result carries { group, ok, choices, usageContract }. Both are read back via getAllSteps + planId match on the done-anchor (helpers/cm2Types.cm2ReadStepResult) — the exact mechanism agentChooseMolecules's own fan-out already uses to read c1, generalized to every subsequent read in this agent.
conventions.writesNothingElse: No molecule, no usage contract, no group index, no todoFrontend/statusFrontend change, no config.json, no materialization. This agent only annotates a page's own .defs.ts — turning that annotation into rendered markup is a future render skill's job, out of scope here.

treeOverview: c1-groups            level 1 -> deterministic regions, LLM decides group or none
c1r-fanout            the root again: plants one c2 per chosen group, plus c3-patch
c2-<group>          level 2 of that group -> LLM decides molecule per region (anti-invention gate)
c3-patch              deterministic: rewrites the target .defs.ts — the run's only write

steps.goal: Extract regions deterministically from the target's dataBindings/inputs (+ sibling contract types) and ask the LLM which published group covers each, or none.

gate.onFail: retry 1 with errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.result: { catalogProject, target, regions: ChRegion[], groups: string[] } — read back by c1r-fanout and c3-patch, never written to disk

steps.goal: Read c1's result from the task tree and plant one c2 per DISTINCT group, plus c3-patch depending on all of them. With no group chosen, c3-patch still runs alone.
For ONE group: choose the molecule for each region c1 assigned to it. Never fails the run — a gate that refuses twice records ok:false and completes anyway.

gate.onFail: retry 1 with errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure records ok:false and completes

steps.result: { group, ok, choices: [{region, tag}], usageContract } — never written to disk

steps.goal: Join c1's regions with every c2 group's accepted choices, patch definition + pipeline, and rewrite the target .defs.ts. Skips the write entirely when nothing changed.

artifacts.the target .defs.ts (rewritten in place): the ONLY file this agent writes — molecule: {group, tag} on dataBindings[]/inputs[], plus pipeline[0].dependsFiles/skills appended with the chosen molecules' source files and usage contract

outOfScope: a molecule-aware render skill (e.g. a future genCfePage12RenderTs.ts) that actually turns `molecule` annotations into markup — this agent only annotates
deciding molecules for 'selection'/'route' inputs — they are never typed, so there is nothing to serve
creating the target file (page12 or any new genome) — the caller decides which file to point this agent at
catalog dependency discovery — the caller must know which project's catalog answers, and pass it explicitly

knownGaps.measuredAgainst: The probe (agentChooseMolecules) run on the same file, _102046_ clientCatalogue/page21: 12 regions to this agent's 7 originally, 11 after the trigger and page-feedback regions. The single one still missing is the destructive confirmation, to which the probe itself answered null.
knownGaps.destructiveConfirmation: The probe's 'Confirmação de exclusão' region, to which it honestly answered group: null — no published group covers a blocking confirmation dialog. Implementing it would only produce another honest null, so the value is in the reporting, not the choice. It also cannot be tied to a specific binding deterministically: knowing cmdDeleteClient is destructive means reading its NAME, which this agent refuses to infer from — though the target's own pageObjective.antiPatterns does declare it in prose ('Tratar exclusão como ação sem confirmação'), so a future version could take it from there. If it lands, its address is `page::confirmation` and it needs no new shape: pageMolecules[] already carries a role.
